- Do not skip ordering just because some incoming exists if IP is low. Day 9 looked okay with 5 on hand + 8 incoming, but Day 10 began with only 2 on hand.

- Ops notes about cycle counts, counts matching, and receiving temp have not affected sales or inventory accuracy so far.

- Previous target IP 24–28 was too low. Use reorder point ~30 and target IP ~40–45. Order daily to bring IP up to target; do not wait.
- Avoid zero stock with no incoming. Days 12–15 and 19–20 had stockouts from late/too-small orders. Order cost is trivial; when IP < ~30, order early.
- Do not skip ordering just because some incoming exists. Day 15 IP was 27 but ordered 0, causing stockout. Day 20 IP was 19 but ordered only 9, causing stockout.

- Ops notes about temp, racking, carrier pickup, and cycle counts have not affected sales or inventory accuracy so far.

Inventory notes (through Day 30)

- Lead time: orders arrive 2 days later. Arrivals field = [today, tomorrow]. IP = on hand + scheduled arrivals.
- Costs: holding ≈ $0.10/unit/day; stockout ≈ $1/unit unmet; ordering $0.50/order. Holding is cheap; stockouts are costly.
- Demand: last 14 recorded sales: 6,10,9,9,10,9,9,17,14,10,6,14,6,6. Since stockouts stopped around Day 23, these are closer to true demand. Typical demand ~9–12/day; spikes 14–17. Earlier sold-out days understated demand.

- Order daily to bring IP up to target. Do not skip when IP < ~30, even if some incoming exists. Day 15/Day 20 errors caused stockouts. Ordering cost is trivial.
- If IP is already ≥ ~35, ordering 0 or small is fine. Day 30: on hand 19, arrivals [14,6], IP = 39; order 0 was correct.
- Recent operation: Days 21–28 kept inventory adequate; no stockouts from Day 23 onward. Holding cost stayed low ($0.40–$2.90/day). Target IP ~38 is working.
- Avoid over-ordering far beyond ~40 unless a demand spike is clearly expected; extra holding is cheap but unnecessary.
- Ops notes (cycle count, temp, racking, carrier pickup, forklift, counts) have not affected sales or inventory accuracy so far.

Inventory notes through Day 40

- Lead time: orders arrive 2 days later. Arrivals = [today, tomorrow]. IP = on hand + scheduled arrivals.
- Costs: holding ≈ $0.10/unit/day; stockout ≈ $1/unit unmet; ordering $0.50/order. Holding is cheap; stockouts are costly.
- Demand: last 14 sales: 6,14,6,6,4,9,9,8,5,9,4,8,1,7. No stockouts since Day 23, so these are closer to true demand. Typical demand now ~4–9/day, occasional spike 14. Earlier 9–12/day estimate is too high for current pattern.
- Policy: target IP ~38 (range 36–40). Order daily to bring IP up to ~38. If IP already ≥ ~37, order 0/small. This avoided stockouts Days 31–40; holding cost was $1.20–$2.60/day, plus $0.50 when ordering.

- Avoid over-ordering far beyond ~40 unless a spike is clearly expected. Extra holding is cheap but unnecessary.

- Recent operation Days 31–40: no stockouts, low costs. Target IP ~38 remains appropriate despite softer demand.

Inventory notes through Day 50

- Lead time: orders arrive 2 days later. Arrivals = [today, tomorrow]. IP = on hand + scheduled arrivals.
- Costs: holding ≈ $0.10/unit/day; stockout ≈ $1/unit unmet; ordering $0.50/order. Stockouts dominate; holding is cheap.
- Demand shifted up. Last 14 sales: 4,8,1,7,8,17,13,8,15,13,10,8,11,13. Typical 8–13/day, spikes 15–21. Earlier 4–9/day estimate and target IP 38 are too low.
- Policy target: raise target IP to ~50 (range 46–55). Order daily to bring IP to ~50. If IP ≥ ~50, order 0/small. If IP < ~45, order up to ~50–52 even if arrivals are already scheduled.
- Reorder point: do not let IP fall below ~45. IP ~38 was insufficient: caused stockouts Days 42–43 and 47–48, costing $4–$10/day. No-stockout days cost only ~$0.50–$1.80.
- Avoid ordering far beyond ~55 unless a sustained spike is clear; extra holding is cheap but unnecessary.
- Ops notes (carrier pickup moved to 3pm, racking rotation, new temp, cycle count) have not affected sales or inventory. Ignore for ordering unless a count shows discrepancy.
- Recent operation: demand is volatile with occasional 17–21 spikes. Safety stock at target IP ~50 is needed to protect against stockouts.

Inventory notes through Day 60

- Lead time: orders arrive 2 days later. IP = on hand + scheduled arrivals over next 2 days (before today’s order).
- Costs: holding ≈ $0.10/unit/day; stockout ≈ $1/unit unmet; ordering $0.50/order. Stockouts hurt, but recent overstock is now costing more than ordering saves.
- Demand last 14 days: 10,8,11,13,9,10,6,16,13,20,6,8,8,5. Typical 6–13/day, occasional 16–20 spikes. Mean ≈10/day; normal 2-day need ≈20.
- Recent Days 51–60: no stockouts, but holding costs rose to $2.90–$3.80/day. Target IP ~50 was too high and caused overstock. Daily small orders to reach 50 are not worth it.
- Revised target: target IP ~45–48, not 50. Reorder point ~40–42.
- Ordering rule: if IP < 40, order up to ~45–48. If IP 40–44, order 0–3 or skip unless clear spike/downtrend. If IP ≥ 45, order 0. Avoid ordering just to hit 50. Do not exceed ~50 unless sustained spike is clear.

- Ops notes (carrier pickup, racking rotation, new temp, cycle count, forklift cert) have not affected sales/inventory. Ignore for ordering unless a count shows discrepancy.

Inventory notes through Day 70

- Lead time: orders arrive 2 days later. IP = on hand + scheduled arrivals over next 2 days, before today’s order.
- Costs: holding ≈ $0.10/unit/day; stockout ≈ $1/unit unmet; ordering $0.50/order. Stockouts hurt, but overstock also costs more than ordering saves.
- Demand last 14 days (Day 70): 6,8,8,5,6,6,7,5,8,10,10,9,4,14. Mean ≈7.6/day. Recent range mostly 4–10, one 14; no 16–20 spikes recently, but earlier spikes show they can return. Normal 2-day need ≈16; with spike, ≈20–25.
- Days 61–70: no stockouts. Holding $1.20–$3.30/day; ordering $0.50 on 7 of 10 days. Total daily cost $1.70–$3.60, avg ≈$2.63. Target IP ~45–48 worked and cut prior overstock without stockouts.
- Keep target IP ~45–47, max ~48 unless clear sustained spike. Reorder point ~40–42.
- Ordering rule: if IP < 40, order up to ~45–47. If IP 40–44, usually order 0 unless clear spike/downtrend. If IP ≥ 45, order 0. Do not exceed ~50 without clear sustained spike.
- Earlier target IP 38 caused stockouts; target 50 overcorrected. IP ~45 has protected against 2-day demand plus normal spikes while lowering holding.
- Ops notes (forklift cert, counts, carrier pickup, racking, temp, cycle count) have not affected sales/inventory. Ignore for ordering unless a count shows discrepancy.
